standard_prerequisites.use: The parent lemma local-local-structure-finite-type (already collected as L16061, which supplies the diagram with geometrically integral fibres and properties (1)-(6)); Morphisms, lemma smooth-open; affineness of finite morphisms over affine targets; fibre products of affines over affines.

core_obligations: Shrink S' to an affine neighbourhood through the smooth open image.
Cut Y' to the affine fibre product piece and verify the geometric-integrality of fibres survives.

proof_roadmap.step: Affine shrinking along the smooth chart.
Affineness propagation through the finite map.

difficulty_reason: Assuming the notation of the chapter's local-local-structure lemma for finite type morphisms (a point x over s with a geometrically unibranch target or quasi-finite source etc., resolved after an elementary etale base change to a finite cover Y' -> X' -> S' with integral fibres), the lemma adds clause (7): S', Y', X' can all be taken affine. The retained proof is written: once Y' is affine, X' is affine because pi : X' -> Y' is finite; choose affine neighbourhoods U' of s' in S' and V' of y' in h^{-1}(U'); the image W' = h(V') is an open neighbourhood of s' (Morphisms, lemma smooth-open); take an affine U'' inside W'; then h^{-1}(U'') cap V' = U'' x_{U'} V' is affine, the restricted smooth map has fibres that are nonempty opens of the geometrically integral fibres of Y' -> S' hence geometrically integral (normality plus connectedness from the parent lemma's construction), so replacing (S', Y') by (U'', h^{-1}(U'') cap V') arranges (7) while preserving (1)-(6). Retained author proof at lines 13532-13545.

dedup.scope: Fully affine form of the local-local structure diagram.
